result.verdict:
**VERDICT: FAIL.** Third consecutive fail. A designer shown these three cold would still guess one process, and this round tells you where the process lives more precisely than either of the first two.

The useful distinction you asked for: **it is both, and the split is measurable.** Where the veto fired it worked, and produced the single largest gain in three rounds. On the ground it was too narrow by exactly one qualifier. Everywhere the convergence actually now lives, it cannot reach, because the thing all three builds agree on is not the ground and is not a colour role. It is the material the signature is cut from, and the ledger does not fingerprint that.

---

## 1. The three arcs, across three rounds

Measured off the rendered pages at 1440 in the browser default scheme. My pipeline reproduces every published number in the two prior reports (R1 ground 17.7≈18.0, R1 surface 6.2≈6.0, R1 accent 30≈29, R1 sat band 18.6 exact, R2 ground 4.1 exact, R2 surface 3.0 exact, R2 sat band 4.5 exact, R2 ink 19.3 exact, luminance spreads 0.301 / 0.387 exact), so the round-three cells are directly comparable rather than re-derived.

| Measure | Round one | Round two | **Round three** |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Ground hue arc** | 17.7° (87.7 / 72.0 / 70.0) | 4.1° (41.1 / 42.0 / 37.9) | **179.4°** (39.2 / 40.0 / 218.6) |
| … the closest pair inside it | 2.0° | 0.9° | **0.8°** (A 39.2, B 40.0) |
| **Raised-surface hue arc** | 6.2° (66.7 / 72.9 / 72.0) | 3.0° (43.6 / 40.6, two sites) | **1.9°** (39.2 / 41.1 / 39.5) |
| **Signature-material hue arc** | not separated from ground | not separated from ground | **0.8°** (39.2 / 40.0 / 39.5) |
| **Most emphatic accent, hue arc** | 30.0° (348.5 / 8.8 / 18.5) | 31.7° (34.1 / 2.4 / 29.4) | **143.3°** (5.5 / 43.9 / 148.8) |
| **… its saturation band** | 18.6 wide (59.5–78.1%) | 4.5 wide (72.9–77.4%) | **38.7 wide (61.3–100%)** |
| Saturated values per build (S≥38%, L 15–70%) | 1 / 1 / 1 | 4 / 2 / 3 | **2 / 2 / 2** |
| Near-black ink arc | 139.5° | 19.3° | 82.0° (but B and C 4.5° apart) |
| Ground luminance spread | 0.301 | 0.387 | **0.573** |
| Display faces | 3 distinct | 3 distinct | 3 distinct (Bevan / Zilla Slab / Grenze) |
| Uppercase elements rendered | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| CSS transitions | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 2 | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| Hairlines (≤1.5px borders) | 28 / 453 / 31 | 32 / 299 / 0 | 0 / 267 / 0 |

Round three's ground and accent arcs are genuinely, hugely wider. Both widenings come from one build each: C's grey cast-metal ground, and C's green accent, which is the one thing in the whole round the veto caused. Strip C out and rounds two and three are the same portfolio: A and B sit at 39.2° and 40.0° on the ground and at 39.2° / 41.1° on the surface.

A second cross-round fact that matters more than any single arc. Blind to earlier rounds, **two of three briefs reproduced their round-two type pairing**: brief A produced Bevan + Newsreader in both rounds, brief B produced Zilla Slab + Archivo in both rounds. Their grounds also landed within 1.9° and 2.0° of their own previous round. The brief plus the instruction surface, not the choice, is doing the work.

## 2. The veto: it fired once, and the build that got it obeyed the purpose, not the letter

`docs/rebuild/s13/ledger/renders.jsonl` holds three accepted entries and no refusals (it only records accepted renders). Six checks were possible (A is first, so 2 checks for B and 4 for C). It fired on one.

**It fired on C, and C complied properly.** From `builds/C/.sitesmith/direction.md`:

> "The first render was refused. The emphatic accent was `--mønje` #8b1f26, red lead, the anti-corrosion primer that goes on ironwork, at hue 356. The ledger measured it 10 degrees from a record already in the book and named 20 degrees as the arc it refuses. It named the region and nothing else, and it was not argued with."

Verified: #8b1f26 is hue 356.1°, A's accent is 5.5°, distance 9.4°, threshold 20°. C did not move two degrees past the arc. It moved 143.3°, changed the noun (red lead to green baize), re-measured contrast from scratch, and changed one dependent rule (`.dæk nav a:active`, which had been taking the accent as text on the metal at 2.5:1 and now takes the dark of the case at 5.1:1). Ground, type, layout, signature and copy untouched, as it says. That is the mechanism working exactly as designed, and it is the sole cause of both accent-axis gains in the table.

**It did not fire on the ground, and B recorded why at the time.** From `builds/B/PRODUCTION-REPORT.md` line 142:

> "Ledgerens ene tidligere post er mid-dark med grundkulør 39 og accentkulør 6. **Grundbåndet er forskelligt, så kulørprøven på grunden gælder ikke**, og accenten ligger 38 grader væk mod en grænse på 20. Ingen nedlæggelse."

B measured its ground at hue 40 against A's 39, saw that the luminance-band qualifier exempted the comparison, wrote that down, and shipped. No dishonesty: the rule genuinely did not apply. But the effect is the thing you asked me to name. **The tightest ground pair in the entire three-round history, 0.8° apart across "reconditioned sewing machines" and "district heating console", passed a veto built specifically to prevent it, and the exemption was noticed and logged at the moment it happened.** Nobody moved two degrees past the arc. The arc did not exist in that band.

A's report confirms the third case: "anti-repeat: ingen veto." A ran first with an empty ledger.

## 3. Where the tell went this round

I checked each candidate against `skills/sitesmith-v3/SKILL.md` before counting it. Things the skill names are **not** evidence: cutting `01/02/03` (§6 line 126 uses that exact example), "not an instrument / the kind the medium reaches for first" (lines 137–141 name the gauge), "specimen" as a kind (line 137 lists it), "let the count fall out of that" (line 110, verbatim), "not a list of roles" (line 106), "spend your boldness in one place" (line 131), "nothing moves between an intent and its result" (lines 134–135, verbatim), the autopilot block (line 84), arguing the runner-up (line 70). All three builds reproduce all of those, several word for word, and none of it counts. It is round two's finding repeating: the fix got written into the always-loaded surface, so now every build quotes the fix.

What nothing forced:

**1. All three signatures are cut from the same colour.** A's `.seddel`, the manila tag, is `hsl(39.2, 25.9%, 62.9%)`. B's `.felt`, the 61 printed boxes of the reading sheet, is `hsl(40.0, 36.6%, 92.0%)`. C's `.bælgelæder`, the hand-cut piece of tawed sheepskin, is `hsl(39.5, 38.6%, 77.6%)`. **A 0.8 degree arc.** Three noun lists with nothing in common (manilakarton, aflæsningsark, alunberedt fåreskind) resolved to one hue. This is the round-three tell and it is the reason the ground veto missed: in A and B the signature material *is* the ground, so the veto would have caught the pair except for the band; in C the material is not the ground at all, so the veto never looked.

**2. All three signatures are one kind again, one slot to the left of round one.** Round one produced three gauges. Round three produces three flat sheets of light warm material with the writing on them: a tag, a sheet, a hide. The skill offers seven kinds (instrument, document, specimen, map, worn surface, machine part, piece of writing set apart). All three picked from the paper end, and four of the seven were taken by nobody. Every one of them justifies it identically, as the artefact the trade already keeps on the bench: A "siden er værkstedets eget logark"; B "which artefact the shift already keeps"; C the condition report the council gets.

**3. A and C both lift that sheet with an irregular cut edge and a large soft shadow.** A: `clip-path: polygon(...)` clipping the tag's top corners plus `box-shadow: 0 7px 16px rgba(12,15,13,0.5)`. C: three hand-cut `clip-path` polygons plus `filter: drop-shadow(0 14px 26px rgba(22,19,14,.42))`. Neither clip-path, nor elevation, nor "lift the panel off the ground" appears anywhere in the skill. These are the two non-console builds, so that is 2 of 2. It is the first thing you see in both 1440 screenshots.

**4. The saturated-value count re-closed at exactly two, and all three announce it.** Measured: 2 / 2 / 2, with a clean gap to the third value in every build (A 71.3, 69.6, then 32.8; B 100, 42.0, then 36.6; C 61.3, 57.1, then 38.6). Across three rounds that is 1/1/1, then 4/2/3, then 2/2/2. The skill forbids one ("a palette with exactly one saturated colour is the default under another name") and says nothing about two. Three builds independently landed on the new minimum and each declared it as the departure: A "der er to mættede farver, ikke én"; B "Seven values, two of them saturated"; C "two of the values are saturated rather than one". Round two's tell was the anti-doctrine stated in one voice. Round three's is the anti-doctrine *counted* to the same number.

**5. A and C both promoted a refusal to a full-bleed band on the page's darkest surface.** A: `<section class="malet">` "Det står der ikke noget om her", five things the page will not claim, on hammerlak. C: `<section class="mørk afvisning">` "Vi sætter ikke elektroniske orgler op", on kassemørke. In both it is the only full-bleed dark band in the body. ## Which of the two, precisely

**Too narrow, by one qualifier, on the axis it owns.** Delete the same-luminance-band condition, or apply the hue arc across bands whenever the two grounds are within a saturation band of each other, and B's 40.0° against A's 39.2° gets refused. That is a one-line change and it would have forced the single most consequential re-choice available in this round. The band qualifier is the whole failure on the ground axis, and B's own report is the receipt.

**And structurally unable to reach the rest.** The fingerprint has six fields: ground, groundHue, accentHue, display, imagery, devices. The convergence that survives round three is in the signature-material hue (0.8°), the raised-surface hue (1.9°, tightening monotonically 6.2 → 3.0 → 1.9 across three rounds while every other axis was being pried open), the saturated-value count, the signature's kind, the clip-path-plus-drop-shadow treatment, the refusal band, the autopilot description and the voice. None of those is the ground. Most are not colours. A veto that names a closed region in hue space cannot name any of them, and widening the arc will not help, because the pair that matters most this round (manila tag at 39.2, reading sheet at 40.0, bellows leather at 39.5) is not three grounds. It is three materials, and only two of them happen to be painted on `body`.

The next mechanism has to fingerprint the signature: its material colour, its kind, and whether it is lifted off the surface behind it. That is measurable from the rendered page with the code already in `portfolio-diversity.mjs`, and it is where three rounds of evidence now say the process lives.
